Magnetic dipole moment of the current loop
$=$ Ampere turns $\times$ Area of the coil or $M=N I \pi r^2$

7152.text:
For the circle $C$ with the equation $x^2+y^2-16 x-12 y+64=0$ match the List I with the List II given below.
The correct match is $\begin{array}{llll}(\mathrm{i}$)& ($\mathrm{ii}) & (\mathrm{iii}$)& ($\mathrm{iv})\end{array}$
7152.sol:
Given equation of circle is

C=x²+y²-16 x-12 y+64=0

(i) Equation of polar at $(-5,1)$ w.r.t. to $C$ is

$\begin{array}{cc}x(-5)+y(1)-8(x-5)-6(y+1)+64=0 \\
\Rightarrow & -5 x+y-8 x+40-6 y-6+64=0 \\
\Rightarrow & -13 x-5 y+98=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 13 x+5 y=98
\end{array}$

(ii) On differentiating Eq. (i) w.r.t.$ to x$, we get

$\begin{array}{rrrr}& 2 x+2 y \frac{d y}{d x}-1$6-12 $\frac{d y}{d x}+$0=0 \\
\Rightarrow & (2 y-12) $\frac{d y}{d x}=(16-2 x) \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{d y}{d x}$=$\left(\frac{8-x}{y-6}$\right)$
\end{array}\text{ At }($8,0) \quad $\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(8,0)}=\frac{8-8}{0-6}$=$0

$\therefore$ Equation of tangent at $(8,0)$ is $(y-0)=0(x-8)$\Rightarrow \quad y=0

(iii) Slope$ of normal is\begin{aligned}$\frac{d y}{d x}$& =$\frac{6-y}{8-x}$\\
$\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(2,6)}$& =$\frac{6-6}{8-2}=$0
\end{aligned}

Equation$ of normal is\begin{aligned}$& & (y-6) & =0(x-2) \\
\Rightarrow & & y & =6
\end{aligned}

\Rightarrow \quad y=6

(iv) Equation$ of the diameter of circle through(8,12)$ is

x=8

10250.text: If the lines $2 x+3 y+12=0, x-y+k=0$ are conjugate with respect to the parabola $y^2=8 x$, then $k$ is equal to
10250.sol:
Given, conjugate lines are
$2 x+3 y+12=0$ ...(i)
and $\quad x-y+k=0$ ...(ii)
We know, that two lines are said to be conjugate with respect to a curve, if each passes through the pole of the polar of that curve. Let $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ be the pole of parabola
$y^2=8 x$
It's polar is $\quad y y_1=4\left(x+x_1\right)\Rightarrow \quad 4 x-y_1 y+4 x_1=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 x-\left(\frac{y_1}{2}\right) y+2 x_1=0$ ...(iii)
On comparing Eqs. (i) and (iii), 
we get $\frac{-y_1}{2}=3 \Rightarrow y_1=-6 and 2 x_1=12 \Rightarrow x_1=6\therefore \quad$ Pole $\left(x_1, y_1\right)=(6,-6)$
Eq. (ii) also passes through pole $(6,-6)\therefore \quad 6-(-6)+k=0\Rightarrow \quad k=-12$

$\dfrac{3x - 2}{( x + 1{)}^{2} ( x + 3 )} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{( x + 1{)}^{2}} + \dfrac{C}{x + 3}$

$\dfrac{3x - 2}{( x + 1{)}^{2} ( x + 3 )} = \dfrac{A ( x + 1 ) ( x + 3 ) + B ( x + 3 ) + C{( x + 1 )}^{2}}{( x + 1{)}^{2} ( x + 3 )}$

$3x - 2 = A ( x^{2} + 3 + 4x ) + B ( x + 3 ) + C ( x^{2} + 1 + 2x )$

$Σ\text{of coefficients of}x^{2} = 0 ⇒ A + C = 0$

$Σ\text{of coefficients of x} = 3 ⇒ 4A + B + 2C = 3$

$Σ\text{of coefficients of constants} = 0 ⇒ 3A + 3B + C = - 2$

Equating the three equations, we get

$A = - C, B = \dfrac{- 2}{5}$

$4A + 2B + 4C = - 5$

Also $|x|+|y|=1\Rightarrow x+y=1, \quad x-y=1x+y=-1, \quad x-y=-1$
Thus solving $x+y=0$ with $x-y=1 or x-y=-1$
We get $\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-1}{2}\right)$ or $\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$
Solving with $x=0$, we get $(0, \pm 1)$
Solving with $y=0$ we get $( \pm 1,0)$
So, we get 6 orderd pairs.

\(\begin{aligned}

\(\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c}}{|\mathbf{a}|}=5 \sqrt{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{p+q-2}{\sqrt{3}}=5 \sqrt{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad p+q-2=15 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad p+q=17 \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}\)
Also, given that \([\mathbf{a} \mathbf{b} \mathbf{c}]=5\)
\(\begin{array}{lrl}
\Rightarrow & {\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & -1 & 1 \\
1 & -2 & 1 \\
p & 2 & q
\end{array}\right]=5} \\
\Rightarrow & 1(-2 q-2)+1(q-p)+1(2+2 p)=5 \\
\Rightarrow & -2 q-2+q-p+2+2 p=5 \\
\Rightarrow & p-q=5 \quad \ldots (ii)
\end{array}\)
By solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get \(p=11, q=6\)
Now,
\(\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{d} & =(\hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \cdot(p \hat{\mathbf{i}}+q \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\
& =p-2 q+2 \\
& =11-12+2 \\
& =1
\end{aligned}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad \tan ^{-1}(\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{d}) & =\tan ^{-1}(\mathbf{l}) \\
& =\tan ^{-1}\left(\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}
\end{aligned}\)

Current density is current per unit area. If we take a circular element of radius $r$ and thickness $d r$, the current through it will be,

$d i = 2\pir d r\beta{\left(r + {r}_{0}\right)}^{2} ⇒ d i = 2\pir d r\beta\left({r}^{2} + 2{r}_{0}r + {{r}_{0}}^{2}\right) ⇒ d i = 2\pi\beta\left({r}^{3} d r + 2{r}_{0}{r}^{2} d r + {{r}_{0}}^{2}r d r\right)$

Integrating the above equation from $0$ to $R$ we will get current through the complete wire.

${∫}_{0}^{I} d i = {∫}_{0}^{R}2\pi\beta\left({r}^{3} d r + 2{r}_{0}{r}^{2} d r + {{r}_{0}}^{2}r d r\right) ⇒ I = 2\pi\beta\left[\dfrac{{R}^{4}}{4} + \dfrac{2{r}_{0}{R}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{{r}_{0}{R}^{2}}{2}\right]$

For current through the shaded area,

$i = \dfrac{\pi}{3 \times \left(2\pi\right)}I = \dfrac{\pi}{3 \times \left(2\pi\right)} \times 2\pi\beta\left[\dfrac{{R}^{4}}{4} + \dfrac{2{r}_{0}{R}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{{r}_{0}{R}^{2}}{2}\right] ⇒ i = \pi\beta\left[\dfrac{{R}^{4}}{12} + \dfrac{2{r}_{0}{R}^{3}}{9} + \dfrac{{r}_{0}{R}^{2}}{6}\right]$

20016.subject: Chemistry
20016.text: Which one of the following Coordination entities exhibits Facial and Meridional isomerism?
20016.sol:
Facial (fac) and Meridional (mer) isomerism is a type of geometric isomerism observed in octahedral complexes of the type $[MA_3B_3]$.

In the complex $\left[\mathrm{Co} \left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_3\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)_3\right], the central metal ion Co is coordinated to three water ligands and three nitrite ligands. This corresponds to the general formula $[MA_3B_3]$.

When the three identical ligands occupy the corners of one triangular face of the octahedron, it is called the facial (fac) isomer. When the three identical ligands occupy positions around the meridian of the octahedron, it is called the meridional (mer) isomer.

The other options provided are not of the $[MA_3B_3]$ type. \left[\mathrm{Co} \left(\mathrm{NH}$}_{3}\right)_4$\mathrm{Br}_{2}\right] \mathrm{NO}$}_{3}$ is of the type $[MA_4B_2]$, which exhibits cis-trans isomerism. \left[\mathrm{Co}(\text{ en })_2 \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}$ is of the type $[M(AA)_2B_2]$, which also exhibits cis-trans isomerism. $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\text{ en })_3\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{3}$ is of the type $[M(AA)_3]$, which exhibits optical isomerism.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Co} \left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\r$ right)_3$\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}\right)_3\right]$

20772.subject: Chemistry
20772.text:
Identify the incorrect statement/s.
A. The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in an atom, in which the largest Principal quantum number value is 4 , is 54 . B. According to Rydberg, all series of lines in Hydrogen spectrum can be described by the equation:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda}=109677   \left(\dfrac{1}{n_1^2}-\dfrac{1}{n_2^2}\right) \mathrm{cm}^{-1}where \left(n_1 \lt n_2\right)$
20772.sol:
For statement A, the maximum number of electrons in an atom with principal quantum number $n=4$ is determined by the total number of orbitals available. The orbitals are $1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 3d, 4s, 4p, 4d, 4f$. The number of orbitals is $1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 3 + 5 + 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 30$. Each orbital can hold 2 electrons, so the maximum capacity is $30 \times 2 = 60$ electrons. Thus, statement A is incorrect.

For statement B, the Rydberg formula for the hydrogen spectrum is given by $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R_H \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right), where $ R_H $\approx109677 \text{ cm}^{-1}. This equation describes all series of lines in the hydrogen spectrum for $ n_1 < n_2$. Thus, statement B is correct.

Answer: Only A$

20843.text: $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ for a reaction are 35.5 kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ and 83.6 J $\textK^{-1}$ respectively. Assuming that $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ do not vary with temperature, the reaction is spontaneous when:
20843.sol:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy must be negative, $\Delta G < 0$.

Using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

For spontaneity:

$\Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$

$T > \dfrac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$

Given values are:

$\Delta H = 35.5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 35500 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta S = 83.6 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1}$

Substituting the values:

$T > \dfrac{35500}{83.6}$

$T > 424.64 \text{ K}$

Therefore, the reaction is spontaneous when $T > 425 \text{ K}$.

Answer: $T > 425\ K$

20969.subject: Mathematics
20969.text: Find the maximum value of $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{4 x^{2}+2 x+1}$.
20969.sol:
To find the maximum value of $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{4x^{2} + 2x + 1}$, we need to find the minimum value of the denominator $g(x) = 4x^{2} + 2x + 1$.

The expression $g(x) = 4x^{2} + 2x + 1$ is a quadratic in the form $ax^{2} + bx + c$ where $a = 4$, $b = 2$, and $c = 1$. Since $a > 0$, the quadratic has a minimum value at $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$.

$x = -\dfrac{2}{2 \times 4} = -\dfrac{2}{8} = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Substituting $x = -\dfrac{1}{4}$ into $g(x)$ to find the minimum value:

$g\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = 4\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{2} + 2\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) + 1 = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{16}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = \dfrac{1 - 2 + 4}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

Since the minimum value of the denominator is $\dfrac{3}{4}$, the maximum value of $f(x)$ is the reciprocal of this minimum value:

$f_\max = \dfrac{1}{3/4} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}$

22101.sol:
The given parallel lines are $8x + 15y - 20 = 0$ and $8x + 15y + 14 = 0$.

The distance between two parallel lines $Ax + By + C_1 = 0$ and $Ax + By + C_2 = 0$ is given by $d = \dfrac{|C_1 - C_2|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}}$.

Substituting $A = 8$, $B = 15$, $C_1 = -20$, and $C_2 = 14$:

$d = \dfrac{|-20 - 14|}{\sqrt{8^2 + 15^2}}$

$d = \dfrac{|-34|}{\sqrt{64 + 225}}$

$d = \dfrac{34}{\sqrt{289}}$

$d = \dfrac{34}{17} = 2$ units.

Answer: $2$ units

Force due to this magnetic field on current carrying wire is given by F=B I L where, $L$ is the length of the wire.

23353.subject: Physics
23353.text: A beam of incident parallel light falls on a diverging lens of focal length 20 cm in magnitude. If a converging lens of focal length 15 cm in magnitude is placed at a distance of 10 cm to the right of the diverging lens on the other side, then, the final image formed is:
options: Virtual and is at a distance of 40 cm to the right of the diverging lens.
Real and is at a distance of 40 cm to the right of the converging lens.
Real and is at a distance of 30 cm to the right of the converging lens.
Virtual and is at a distance of 30 cm to the right of the converging lens.
23353.sol:
For the diverging lens, the focal length $f_1 = -20$ cm. Since the incident light is parallel, the rays appear to diverge from the focus of the diverging lens located at $20$ cm to the left of the lens. The image formed by the first lens acts as the object for the second lens.

The position of this virtual object for the second lens is $10$ cm (distance between lenses) $+ 20$ cm (focal length of first lens) $= 30$ cm to the left of the converging lens. Thus, $u_2 = -30$ cm.

For the converging lens, the focal length $f_2 = +15$ cm. Using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$, we have $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{15}$.

Solving for $v_2$: $\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{2-1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$.

Therefore, $v_2 = +30$ cm. The positive sign indicates that the image is real and formed at a distance of $30$ cm to the right of the converging lens.

Answer: Real and is at a distance of 30 cm to the right of the converging lens.

23574.subject: Physics
23574.text: In an adiabatic expansion of air, the volume is increased by $6.2 \%$. The percentage change in pressure is $(\gamma=1.4)$
23574.sol:
For an adiabatic process, the relation between pressure $P$ and volume $V$ is given by $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

Taking the logarithmic differentiation of the equation $PV^{\gamma} = C$, we get $\ln P + \gamma \ln V = \ln C$.

Differentiating both sides, we obtain $\dfrac{dP}{P} + \gamma \dfrac{dV}{V} = 0$, which implies $\dfrac{dP}{P} = -\gamma \dfrac{dV}{V}$.

Given that the volume increases by $6.2 \%$, we have $\dfrac{dV}{V} = 0.062$.

Substituting the values $\gamma = 1.4$ and $\dfrac{dV}{V} = 0.062$ into the expression for the fractional change in pressure:

$\dfrac{dP}{P} = -1.4 \times 0.062 = -0.0868$.

The percentage change in pressure is $\dfrac{dP}{P} \times 100 = -0.0868 \times 100 = -8.68 \%$.

The magnitude of the percentage change in pressure is $8.68 \%$.

Answer: 8.68

Given values are $Q = 150 \text{ J}$ and $W = 110 \text{ J}$.

Substituting these values into the equation:

$\Delta U = 150 \text{ J} - 110 \text{ J} = 40 \text{ J}$

Answer: 40 J

24076.text: What is the ratio of the velocity of an electron in the fourth orbit of $\text{Be}^{3+}$ to the velocity of the electron in the second orbit of $\text{He}^+$?
24076.sol:
The velocity of an electron in the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen-like ion is given by $v \propto \dfrac{Z}{n}$.

For $\text{Be}^{3+}$, $Z = 4$ and $n = 4$.

$v_{\text{Be}^{3+}} \propto \dfrac{4}{4} = 1$

For $\text{He}^{+}$, $Z = 2$ and $n = 2$.

$v_{\text{He}^{+}} \propto \dfrac{2}{2} = 1$

The ratio of their velocities is $\dfrac{v_{\text{Be}^{3+}}}{v_{\text{He}^{+}}} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1:1$.

Answer: $1:1$

Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of all real numbers. Let $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ and $g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow(0,4)$ be functions defined by $f(x)=\log _e\left(x^2+2 x+4\right)$, and $g(x)=\frac{4}{1+e^{-2 x}}$

25863.text:
Let $\mathbb{R}^2$ denote $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}. Let $S=$\left\{(a, b, c): a, b, c \in \mathbb{R} \text{$ and } a x^2+2 b x y+c y^2>0 $\text{ for $all }(x, y) \in$\mathbb{R}^2-$\{(0,0)\}\right\} .$
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?$
options:
For any given $(a, b, c) \in S$, the system of linear equations
$\begin{aligned}& a x+b y=1 \\& b x+c y=-1\end{aligned}$ 
has a unique solution.

For any given $(a, b, c) \in S$, the system of linear equations
$\begin{aligned}& (a+1) x+b y=0 \\& b x+(c+1) y=0\end{aligned}$
has a unique solution.
25863.sol:
\(\begin{aligned}
& a x^2+2 b x y+c y^2>0 \\
& y, x \in \mathbb{R}-\{(0,0)\} \\
& \Rightarrow c\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^2+2 b\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+a>0 \\
& 4 b^2-4 a c<0 \\
& \Rightarrow b^2<a c
\end{aligned}\)
(A) \(\left(2, \frac{7}{2}, 6\right)\)
\(\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2>2 \times 6\)
\(\therefore\) option A is incorrect
\(\begin{aligned}
& \text{(B) if }\left(3, b, \frac{1}{12}\right) \in S \\
& \Rightarrow b^2<3 \cdot \frac{1}{12} \\
& \Rightarrow b^2<\frac{1}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow 4 b^2<1 \\
& \Rightarrow|2 b|<1 \text{ option } B \text{ is correct }
\end{aligned}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \text{(C) } a x+b y=1 \\
& b x+c y=-1 \\
& D=\left|\begin{array}{ll}
a & b \\
b & c
\end{array}\right|=a c-b^2 \neq 0
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) unique solution option C is correct.
\(\begin{aligned}
& \text{(D) }(a+1) \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{by}=0 \\
& \mathrm{bx}+(\mathrm{c}+1) \mathrm{y}=0 \\
& D=\left|\begin{array}{cc}
(a+1) & b \\
b & (c+1)
\end{array}\right| \\
& =(a+1)(c+1)-b^2 \\
& \Rightarrow a c-b^2+a+c+1 \\
& b^2<a c \Rightarrow a c \text{ is +ve } \\
& \Rightarrow a \text{ and care positive then }\left(a c-b^2\right)+a+c+1>0
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) unique solution
\(\therefore\) option D is correct.

28052.text:
Water decomposes at $2300K$

${H}_{2}O\left(g\right) \to {H}_{2}\left(g\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2}\left(g\right)$

The percent of water decomposing at $2300K$ and 1 bar is _____ (Nearest integer). Equilibrium constant for the reaction is $2 \times {10}^{- 3}$ at $2300K$
28052.sol:
Decomposition of water gives:
${H}_{2}O\left(g\right) ⇌ {H}_{2}\left(g\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2}\left(g\right)$

${P}_{0}\left[1 - \alpha\right]{P}_{0}\alpha\dfrac{{P}_{0}\alpha}{2}$ partial pr. at eq.

Thus, ${P}_{0}\left[1 + \dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right] = 1 \ldots \left(1\right)$

${K}_{p} = \dfrac{\left({P}_{{H}_{2}}\right){\left({P}_{{O}_{2}}\right)}^{1 / 2}}{{P}_{{H}_{2}O}}$

$\dfrac{\left({P}_{0}\alpha\right){\left(\dfrac{{P}_{0}\alpha}{2}\right)}^{1 / 2}}{{P}_{0}\left[1 - \alpha\right]} = 2 \times {10}^{- 3}$

since $\alpha$ is negligible w.r.t 1 thus, $1 - \alpha \approx 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha\sqrt{\alpha}}{\sqrt{2}} = 2 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{3 / 2} = {2}^{3 / 2} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ \alpha = {2}^{3 / 2 \times 2 / 3} \times {10}^{- 3 \times 2 / 3}$

$⇒ \alpha = 2 \times {10}^{- 2}, % \alpha = 2 %$

30466.text: Identify product A and product B
30466.sol:
The allylic position is a carbon position present adjacent to the carbon-carbon double bonds. The allylic carbon is attached to a carbon atom that forms a double bond with a different carbon atom. A substitution could be a reaction during which a group in an organic molecule is replaced with another group.

When the halogen concentration is low enough, alkenes containing allylic hydrogen undergo substitution at the allylic position rather than addition at the double bond. The product is an allylic halide (halogen on carbon next to double bond carbons), which is acquired through a radical chain mechanism.

When cyclohexene reacts with Chlorine in the presence of ${CCl}_{4}$, the electrophilic addition reaction takes place at double bond, which results in a dichloro product, here it is $1, 2 -$dicholorocyclohexane.

Hence, the correct answer is D.

$T$ is the temperature

Conditions for spontaneous and non spontaneous reactions in terms of free energy change are as follows,

 $\Delta G >0$for non-sponateneous reaction

$\Delta G < 0$for spontaneous reaction.

$( \Delta G{)}_{P, T} = ( + ) ve$ for non-spontaneous process

33253.subject: Mathematics
33253.text: The sum of squares of all the real solutions of the equation $\log_{(x+1)}(2x^2+5x+3) = 4 - \log_{(2x+3)}(x^2+2x+1)$ is equal to ________.
33253.sol:
For the logarithms to be defined, we must satisfy the following conditions:
1. Base of the first logarithm: $x+1 > 0 \Rightarrow x > -1$ and $x+1 eq 1 \Rightarrow x eq 0$.
2. Base of the second logarithm: $2x+3 > 0 \Rightarrow x > -\dfrac{3}{2}$ and $2x+3 eq 1 \Rightarrow x eq -1$.
3. Arguments must be positive: $2x^2+5x+3 > 0$ and $x^2+2x+1 > 0$.
Taking the intersection of all these conditions, the domain of the equation is $x \in (-1, 0) \cup (0, \infty)$.

Now, factorizing the arguments of the logarithms:
$2x^2+5x+3 = (2x+3)(x+1)$
$x^2+2x+1 = (x+1)^2$

Substitute these into the given equation:
$\log_{(x+1)}((2x+3)(x+1)) = 4 - \log_{(2x+3)}((x+1)^2)$

Using the properties of logarithms:
$\log_{(x+1)}(2x+3) + \log_{(x+1)}(x+1) = 4 - 2\log_{(2x+3)}(x+1)$
$\log_{(x+1)}(2x+3) + 1 = 4 - \dfrac{2}{\log_{(x+1)}(2x+3)}$

Let $t = \log_{(x+1)}(2x+3)$. The equation becomes:
$t + 1 = 4 - \dfrac{2}{t}$
$t - 3 + \dfrac{2}{t} = 0$
$t^2 - 3t + 2 = 0$
$(t-1)(t-2) = 0$
$\Rightarrow t = 1$ or $t = 2$

Case 1: $t = 1$
$\log_{(x+1)}(2x+3) = 1$
$2x+3 = x+1$
$x = -2$
This value is rejected because $x = -2$ does not fall in the domain $x > -1$.

Case 2: $t = 2$
$\log_{(x+1)}(2x+3) = 2$
$2x+3 = (x+1)^2$
$2x+3 = x^2+2x+1$
$x^2 = 2$
$x = \pm\sqrt{2}$

Since $x > -1$, $x = -\sqrt{2}$ is rejected. The only valid solution is $x = \sqrt{2}$.

The sum of squares of all the real solutions is $(\sqrt{2})^2 = 2$.

Answer: $2$

34713.subject: Mathematics
34713.text: Let the tangent at any point $P$ on a curve passing through the points $\left(1, 1\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{1}{10}, 100\right)$, intersect positive $x$-axis and $y$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$ respectively. If $PA: PB = 1: k$ and $y = y\left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation $e\dfrac{dy}{dx} = kx + \dfrac{k}{2}, y\left(0\right) = k$, then $4y\left(1\right) - 5{\log}_{e}3$ is equal to _______________
34713.sol:
Given,

The tangent at any point $P$ on a curve passing through the points $\left(1, 1\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{1}{10}, 100\right)$, intersect positive $x$-axis and $y$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$ respectively,

And $PA: PB = 1: k$ and $y = y\left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation $e\dfrac{dy}{dx} = kx + \dfrac{k}{2}, y\left(0\right) = k$,

Now on plotting the diagram we get,

Equation of tangent at $P\left(x, y\right)$ is :

$Y - y = \dfrac{dy}{dx}\left(X - x\right)$

Coordinate of $A = \left(x - y\dfrac{dx}{dy}, 0\right)$

Coordinate of $B = \left(0, y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)$

$∴ \left(x, y\right) = \left(\dfrac{kx - ky\dfrac{dx}{dy}}{k + 1}, \dfrac{y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}}{k + 1}\right)$

So, $y = \dfrac{y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}}{k + 1}$

$⇒ y\left(k + 1\right) = y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ ky = - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ k\dfrac{dx}{x} = - \dfrac{dy}{y}$

Now integrating both side, we get

$kln | x | + ln | y | = lnC . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now given equation $\left(i\right)$ passes through $\left(1, 1\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{1}{10}, 100\right)$

So, $C = 1$ and $k = 2$

Now putting the value of $k$, we get

$e\dfrac{dy}{dx} = kx + \dfrac{k}{2}$

$⇒ e\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x + 1\left\{\text{as}k = 2\right\}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = ln\left(2x + 1\right)$

Integrating the above equation we get,

$y = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2x + 1\right)\left(ln\left|2x + 1\right| - 1\right) + C$

And the above equation passes through $\left(0, 2\right)$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{5}{2}$

So, $2y = \left(2x + 1\right)\left(ln\left|2x + 1\right| - 1\right) + 5$

$⇒ 2y\left(1\right) = 3\left(ln3 - 1\right) + 5$

$⇒ 2y\left(1\right) = 3ln\left(3\right) + 2$

Hence, $4y\left(1\right) - 5{\log}_{e}3 = 2\left[3ln3 + 2\right] - 5ln3$

$⇒ 4y\left(1\right) - 5{\log}_{e}3 = 6ln3 + 4 - 5ln3$

$⇒ 4y\left(1\right) - 5{\log}_{e}3 = 4 + ln3 \approx 5$

Note: This question was bonus in Jee Mains 2023 April session.

35455.text: The equation of a tangent to the hyperbola, $4{x}^{2} - 5{y}^{2} = 20,$ parallel to the line $x - y = 2,$ is
35455.sol:
The slope of a line $ax + by + c = 0$ is $m = - \dfrac{a}{b} .$

Thus, the slope of the line $x - y = 2$ is $m = - \dfrac{1}{\left(- 1\right)} = 1$ and we know that if two lines are parallel then their slopes are equal, hence the slope of the tangent is also $m = 1 .$

The given hyperbola is $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{5} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{4} = 1$

The equation of the tangent to the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ having slope $m$ is $y = mx \pm \sqrt{{a}^{2}{m}^{2} - {b}^{2}} .$

Hence, the equation of its tangent having slope $1$ is $y = x \pm \sqrt{5 \times {1}^{2} - 4}$

$⇒ y = x \pm 1$

Thus, the tangents are $x - y + 1 = 0 \text{ and } x - y - 1 = 0 .$

36250.sol:
Let $\alpha = \dfrac{1}{5}cos\theta, \beta = \dfrac{1}{2}sin\theta$

After eliminating ${m}_{1} and {m}_{2}$, we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{- 5 \pm \sqrt{29}}{2} ⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{54 \pm 10\sqrt{29}}{4}$

i.e. $\alpha = \dfrac{- 5 \pm \sqrt{29}}{10} ⇒ 10\alpha + 5 = \pm \sqrt{29}$

and ${\beta}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}\sin^{2}\theta ⇒ 16{\beta}^{2} = - 50 \pm 10\sqrt{29}$

Hence, ${\left(10\alpha + 5\right)}^{2} + {\left(16{\beta}^{2} + 50\right)}^{2} = 2929$

37444.text: Let ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ be two relations defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by $a{R}_{1}b ⇔ ab \ge 0$ and $a{R}_{2}b ⇔ a \ge b$, then

37444.sol:
Given,

${R}_{1} = \left\{ab \ge 0, a, b \in R\right\}$

For reflexive $a \times a \ge 0$ which is true,

For symmetric

If $ab \ge 0 ⇒ ba \ge 0$ which is true,

If $a = 2, b = 0$ and $c = - 2$

Then $a \cdot b \ge 0$ and $b \cdot c \ge 0$ but $a \cdot c \ge 0$ is not true

$⇒$ not transitive relation

$⇒ {R}_{1}$ is not equivalence

For ${R}_{2}$ if $a \ge b$ it does not implies $b \ge a$

$⇒ {R}_{2}$ is not equivalence relation

So, neither ${R}_{1}$ nor ${R}_{2}$ is an equivalence relation

37876.subject: Mathematics
37876.text:
Let a line $L_1$ pass through the origin and be perpendicular to the lines
$L_2: \vec{r} = (3+t)\hat{i} + (2t-1)\hat{j} + (2t+4)\hat{k}$ and
$L_3: \vec{r} = (3+2s)\hat{i} + (3+2s)\hat{j} + (2+s)\hat{k}$, $t, s \in \mathbb{R}$.
If $(a, b, c)$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, is the point on $L_3$ at a distance of $\sqrt{17}$ from the point of intersection of $L_1$ and $L_2$, then $(a+b+c)^2$ is equal to ________.
37876.sol:
The direction vectors of the given lines $L_2$ and $L_3$ are $\vec{d_2} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{d_3} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ respectively.

Since line $L_1$ is perpendicular to both $L_2$ and $L_3$, its direction vector $\vec{d_1}$ is given by the cross product of $\vec{d_2}$ and $\vec{d_3}$:
$\vec{d_1} = \vec{d_2} \times \vec{d_3} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$

Since $L_1$ passes through the origin, its equation is:
$\vec{r} = \lambda(-2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$

Let the point of intersection of $L_1$ and $L_2$ be $P$. The coordinates of $P$ can be written as $(-2\lambda, 3\lambda, -2\lambda)$ from $L_1$ and $(3+t, 2t-1, 2t+4)$ from $L_2$. Equating the respective coordinates:
$-2\lambda = 3 + t$
$3\lambda = 2t - 1$
$-2\lambda = 2t + 4$

From the first and third equations, we get:
$3 + t = 2t + 4 \Rightarrow t = -1$

Substituting $t = -1$ into the first equation gives $-2\lambda = 2 \Rightarrow \lambda = -1$. This also satisfies the second equation. Thus, the point of intersection is $P(2, -3, 2)$.

Let the point on $L_3$ be $Q(a, b, c) = (3+2s, 3+2s, 2+s)$. The distance between $P$ and $Q$ is given as $\sqrt{17}$.
$PQ^2 = 17$
$(3+2s - 2)^2 + (3+2s - (-3))^2 + (2+s - 2)^2 = 17$
$(2s + 1)^2 + (2s + 6)^2 + s^2 = 17$
$4s^2 + 4s + 1 + 4s^2 + 24s + 36 + s^2 = 17$
$9s^2 + 28s + 37 = 17$
$9s^2 + 28s + 20 = 0$
$9s^2 + 18s + 10s + 20 = 0$
$(9s + 10)(s + 2) = 0$

This gives $s = -2$ or $s = -\dfrac{10}{9}$.

Since $a = 3 + 2s$ must be an integer ($a \in \mathbb{Z}$), we must choose $s = -2$.

Substituting $s = -2$ into the coordinates of $Q$:
$a = 3 + 2(-2) = -1$
$b = 3 + 2(-2) = -1$
$c = 2 + (-2) = 0$

Therefore, $(a, b, c) = (-1, -1, 0)$.

We need to find the value of $(a+b+c)^2$:
$(a+b+c)^2 = (-1 - 1 + 0)^2 = (-2)^2 = 4$

Answer: $4$

39368.text: Three blocks $A, B$ and $C$ are lying on a smooth horizontal surface, as shown in the figure. $A$ and $B$ have equal masses, $m$ while $C$ has mass $M .$ Block $A$ is given an initial speed $v$ towards $B$ due to which it collides with $B$ perfectly inelastically. The combined mass collides with $C,$ also perfectly inelastically . $\dfrac{5}{6}\text{t}\text{h}$ of the initial kinetic energy is lost in the whole process. What is the value of $M / m$?
39368.sol:
$mv = \left(m + m\right){v}^{′}$

$\left(m + m\right){v}^{′} = \left(m + m + M\right){v}_{f}$

$∴$ final velocity ${v}_{f} = \dfrac{m}{2m + M}v$

Initial energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Final energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m + M\right){\left(\dfrac{mv}{2m + M}\right)}^{2}$

Given that $\dfrac{5}{6}\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m + M\right){\left(\dfrac{mv}{2m + M}\right)}^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{12}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{m}^{2}{v}^{2}}{\left(2m + M\right)}$

$6m = 2m + M$

$\dfrac{M}{m} = 4$

40811.subject: Physics
40811.text: A planet $(P_1)$ is moving around the star of mass $2M$ in the orbit of radius $R$. Another planet $(P_2)$ is moving around another star of mass $4M$ in a orbit of radius $2R$. Ratio of time periods of revolution of $P_2$ and $P_1$ is _______.
40811.sol:
Using Kepler's third law, the time period of revolution of a planet is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM_s}}$.

For planet $P_1$, the orbital radius is $r = R$ and the mass of the star is $M_s = 2M$:
$T_1 = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{G(2M)}}$

For planet $P_2$, the orbital radius is $r = 2R$ and the mass of the star is $M_s = 4M$:
$T_2 = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{(2R)^3}{G(4M)}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{8R^3}{4GM}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{2R^3}{GM}}$

Taking the ratio of $T_2$ and $T_1$:
$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{2R^3}{GM}}}{\sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{2GM}}} = \sqrt{2 \times 2} = 2$

Answer: $2$

The densities of materials are in the ratio $3: 5$. The moment of inertia of these discs respectively about their diameters will be in the ratio of $\dfrac{x}{6}$. The value of $x$ is ______.

Mass of the disc in terms of density can be written as, $m = ρ\left(\pi{R}^{2}t\right)$.

$⇒ {R}^{2} = \dfrac{m}{ρ\pit}$

Now moment of inertia of the disc about the diameter is, $\dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{4}$.

Required ratio, $\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{2}{t}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1}{t}_{1}} = \dfrac{5}{3} \times \dfrac{0 . 5}{1} = \dfrac{5}{6}$

Hence, $x = 5$.

44041.subject: Physics
44041.text: The percentage error in the calculated volume of a sphere, if there is $2\%$ error in its diameter measurement, is __________.
44041.sol:
The volume of a sphere in terms of its diameter $D$ is given by $V = \dfrac{\pi}{6}D^3$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides, we get $\ln V = \ln\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + 3 \ln D$

Differentiating for small errors, we obtain $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = 3 \dfrac{\Delta D}{D}$

Multiplying by $100$ to find the percentage error, $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = 3 \left(\dfrac{\Delta D}{D} \times 100\right)$

Given that the percentage error in the diameter is $2\%$, we have $\dfrac{\Delta D}{D} \times 100 = 2$

Therefore, the percentage error in the volume is $3 \times 2 = 6\%$

Answer: $6$

The displacement equation is given by
$x=a_0+\frac{a_1 t}{2}-\frac{a_2 t^2}{3}$
Velocity $=$ rate of change of displacement
ie, $\quad v=\frac{d x}{d t} \begin{aligned} & =\frac{d}{d t}\left(a_0+\frac{a_1 t}{2}-\frac{a_2 t^2}{3}\right) \\ & =0+\frac{a_1}{2}-\frac{2 a_2 t}{3} \\ & =\frac{a_1}{2}-\frac{2 a_2 t}{3}\end{aligned}$
Acceleration $=$ rate of change of velocity
$i e$, 
$\begin{aligned} a & =\frac{d v}{d t} \\ & =\frac{d}{d t}\left(\frac{a_1}{2}-\frac{2 a_2}{3} t\right) \\ & =0-\frac{2 a_2}{3} \\ & =-\frac{2 a_2}{3}\end{aligned}$

46979.sol: Thymus gland is found in the upper part of thorax near the heart. It is a bilobed pinkish gland. At the time of birth, it is a prominent gland but in the adult it gradually atrophies. 47295.subject: Biology
47295.text:
Read the following statements.
Statement I: In a typical test cross, an organism showing a dominant phenotype is crossed with the recessive parent.
Statement II: The ratio of organisms showing dominant and recessive traits in $F_1$ generation of a test cross indicates that the organism with unknown genotype is homozygous dominant.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
47295.sol:
Statement I is true because a test cross is performed to determine the genotype of an organism exhibiting a dominant phenotype by crossing it with a homozygous recessive parent.

Statement II is false because if the $F_1$ generation of a test cross produces both dominant and recessive phenotypes (typically in a $1:1$ ratio), it indicates that the organism with the unknown genotype is heterozygous, not homozygous dominant. If the unknown organism were homozygous dominant, all $F_1$ offspring would exhibit only the dominant phenotype.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

55982.subject: Chemistry
55982.text: What is the time required for 75 % completion of a first order reaction if rate constant is $23.03\ \text{minute}^{-1}$ ?
55982.sol:
For a first order reaction, the time required for a given completion is given by:

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a-x} \right)

Given $ k = 23.03 $\text{ min}^{-1} and for 75\%$ completion, $x = 0.75a$.

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{23.03} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a - 0.75a} \right)$

$t = 0.1 \log \left( \dfrac{1}{0.25} \right)$

$t = 0.1 \log 4$

$t = 0.1 \times0.602 = 0.0602 \text{ min}$

Converting the time into seconds:

$t = 0.0602 \times60 \text{ s} =3.612 \text{ s} \approx3.6 \text{ s}$

Answer: $3.6$ s

56629.text: Which actinoid from following has smallest ionic size in $+3$ state?
56629.sol:
In the actinoid series, as the atomic number increases from Actinium (Ac) to Lawrencium (Lr), there is a gradual decrease in the size of atoms or $M^{3+}$ ions. This phenomenon is known as actinoid contraction, which is due to the poor shielding effect of the $5f$ electrons.

The given elements belong to the actinoid series with the following atomic numbers:
Pa (Z = 91$)
Cm (Z = 96$)
Fm (Z = 100$)
Lr (Z = 103$)

Since Lawrencium (Lr) has the highest atomic number among the given options, it experiences the maximum actinoid contraction. Therefore, $Lr^{3+}$ has the smallest ionic size.

Answer: Lr

57175.subject: Chemistry
57175.text: Which of the following compounds is an optically inactive compound?
57175.sol:
Optical inactivity arises in achiral molecules. A compound lacking chiral centers or possessing a plane of symmetry is achiral and thus optically inactive.

For 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, the carbon at position 2 is bonded to $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, with two identical methyl groups making it non-chiral. No other chiral centers exist, and the molecule lacks a plane of symmetry, confirming achirality.

In contrast, 3-chlorohexane has one chiral center at $C3$ with groups $- \text{H}$, $- \text{Cl}$, $- \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and $- \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, all distinct. 2-chloropentane and 2-chloro-3-methylbutane each possess a chiral center at $C2$, bonded to distinct groups, ensuring chirality and optical activity.

Only 2-chloro-2-methylbutane is achiral and optically inactive.

57960.subject: Chemistry
57960.text: A weak base is $1.3\%$ dissociated in its aqueous solution. If $K_b$ for weak base is $1.69 \times 10^{-5}$ at $298$ K. Find the concentration of aqueous solution of weak base.
57960.sol:
For a weak base, the dissociation constant $K_b$ is given by Ostwald's dilution law:

$K_b = \dfrac{C \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$

Since the degree of dissociation $\alpha = 1.3\% = 0.013$ is very small ($\alpha \ll 1$), we can approximate $1 - \alpha \approx 1$. The expression simplifies to:

$K_b = C \alpha^2$

Rearranging for concentration $C$:

$C = \dfrac{K_b}{\alpha^2}$

Substituting the given values $K_b = 1.69 \times 10^{-5}$ and $\alpha = 0.013$:

$C = \dfrac{1.69 \times 10^{-5}}{(0.013)^2}$

$C = \dfrac{1.69 \times 10^{-5}}{1.69 \times 10^{-4}}$

$C = 10^{-1} = 0.1$ M

Answer: $0.1$ M

58723.subject: Chemistry
58723.text: Identify the elements of alkali metals and alkaline earth metals respectively having highest 1st ionization enthalpy.
58723.sol:
Ionization enthalpy decreases down a group in the periodic table due to an increase in atomic size and shielding effect.

Among alkali metals (Group 1), Lithium ($\text{Li}$) is at the top of the group and has the smallest atomic size, hence it has the highest first ionization enthalpy.

Among alkaline earth metals (Group 2), Beryllium ($\text{Be}$) is at the top of the group and has the smallest atomic size, hence it has the highest first ionization enthalpy.

Therefore, the elements with the highest first ionization enthalpy are $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Be}$ respectively.

Answer: $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Be}$

58870.text: Calculate the volume occupied by a particle in bcc unit cell if the volume of unit cell is $8.2 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ cm}^3$
58870.sol:
Volume occupied by a single atom in a BCC unit cell

Given the unit cell volume $V_{\text{unit cell}} = 8.2 \times 10^{-23} \ \mathrm{cm}^3$, and since the BCC structure contains $Z = 2$ atoms per unit cell with packing efficiency $\mathrm{PE} = 0.68$, the volume per atom is derived from the relation:

$V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{\mathrm{PE} \times V_{\text{unit cell}}}{Z}$

Substituting the values:

$V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{0.68 \times 8.2 \times 10^{-23}}{2} = 2.788 \times 10^{-23} \ \mathrm{cm}^3$

The result corresponds to option C.

61743.sol:
$y=(1+x)\left(1+x^2\right)\left(1+x^4\right)\left(1+x^8\right)...(i)$
Taking 'log' on both sides, we get $\begin{aligned} & \log y=\log (1+x)+\log \left(1+x^2\right)+\log \left(1+x^4\right) \\ &+ \log \left(1+x^8\right) \end{aligned}$

61967.subject: Mathematics
61967.text: The equations of the tangents to the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1$ making an inclination of $30^{}^{\circ}$ with the major axis are
61967.sol:
The equation of the ellipse is $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1$.

Here, $a^2 = 16$ and $b^2 = 9$.

The tangent makes an angle of $30^{}^{\circ}$ with the major axis (x-axis), so the slope of the tangent is $m = \tan 30^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

The equation of the tangent to the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ with slope $m$ is given by $y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 + b^2}$.

Substituting the values of $a^2$, $b^2$, and $m$, we get:

$y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x \pm \sqrt{16\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 + 9}$

$y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{3} + 9}$

$y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{16 + 27}{3}}$

$y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{43}{3}}$

Multiplying the entire equation by $\sqrt{3}$, we obtain:

$\sqrt{3}y = x \pm \sqrt{43}$

$x - \sqrt{3}y \pm \sqrt{43} = 0$

Answer: $x - \sqrt{3}\,y \pm \sqrt{43} = 0$

63168.sol:
Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$

The determinant of $A$ is $|A| = (3)(4) - (-2)(1) = 12 + 2 = 14$

The adjugate of $A$ is $\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$

The inverse of $A$ is given by $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \text{adj}(A)$

$A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{14} \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{4}{14} & \dfrac{2}{14} \\ -\dfrac{1}{14} & \dfrac{3}{14} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{2}{7} & \dfrac{1}{7} \\ -\dfrac{1}{14} & \dfrac{3}{14} \end{bmatrix}$

Answer: $\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{2}{7} & \dfrac{1}{7} \\ -\dfrac{1}{14} & \dfrac{3}{14} \end{bmatrix}$

63504.subject: Mathematics
63504.text: A regular polygon has 20 sides. The number of triangles that can be drawn by using the vertices but not using the sides are
63504.sol:
The number of triangles formed from vertices of a regular 20-gon without using polygon sides equals the count of triangles that share no sides with the polygon.

The total number of triangles is given by $C(20,3) = \frac{20 \times 19 \times 18}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 1140$.

Triangles sharing exactly two sides correspond to three consecutive vertices, yielding $20$ such triangles.
Triangles sharing exactly one side are formed by selecting one side (20$ choices) and a non-adjacent third vertex (20 - 4 = 16$ choices), giving $20 \times 16 = 320$ triangles.

The count of triangles sharing no sides is then $1140 - (20 + 320) = 800$.

Final answer: $\boxed{800}$

& \text{ Consider } \\

65587.text: An a.c. circuit contains resistance of $12 \Omega$ and inductor of inductive reactance $5 \Omega$. The phase angle between current and potential difference will be
65587.sol:
The phase angle $\phi$ between current and potential difference in an AC circuit with resistance $R = 12\,\Omega$ and inductive reactance $X_L = 5\,\Omega$ satisfies $\tan \phi = \frac{X_L}{R} = \frac{5}{12}$.

The impedance is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{144 + 25} = 13\,\Omega$.

From the impedance triangle, $\cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{12}{13}$ and $\sin \phi = \frac{X_L}{Z} = \frac{5}{13}$.

Therefore, $\phi = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{13}\right)$ or equivalently $\phi = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)$.

Comparing with the given options, the correct expression is $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{13}\right)$ which corresponds to option D.

66561.subject: Physics
66561.text: If $E_p$ and $E_e$ represent kinetic energy of photon and electron respectively. If de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_p$ of a photon is twice the de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_e$ of electron, then $E_e / E_p$ is (Speed of electron $=\frac{\mathrm{C}}{100}$, where 'C' is the velocity of light)
66561.sol:
The ratio $E_e / E_p$ is derived from the kinetic energies of an electron and photon sharing equivalent de-Broglie wavelengths, with the electron moving at $v_e = C/100$.

For a photon, the de-Broglie wavelength gives momentum $p_p = E_p/C$, so $E_p = hC/\lambda_p$.

For the electron, $p_e = m_e v_e = h/\lambda_e$, and its kinetic energy is $E_e = \frac{1}{2} m_e v_e^2$. Substituting, $E_e = \frac{1}{2} (h/\lambda_e) v_e$.

The ratio becomes:

$\frac{E_e}{E_p} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{v_e}{C} \cdot \frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e}$

Given $\lambda_p = 2\lambda_e$ and $v_e = C/100$, substitution yields:

$\frac{E_e}{E_p} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{100} \cdot 2 = \frac{1}{100}$

Final Answer: $\boxed{1 \times 10^{-2}}$

Area of the disc, $A = \pi r^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times (0.2)^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 0.04 \text{ m}^2$

Magnetic field, $B = \dfrac{7}{22} \text{ Wb/m}^2$

Angle between the axis of the disc (area vector) and the magnetic field, $\theta = 60^{}^{\circ}$

Magnetic flux linked with the disc is given by $\Phi = B A \cos \theta$

Substituting the values:

$\Phi = \dfrac{7}{22} \times \left( \dfrac{22}{7} \times 0.04 \right) \times \cos 60^{}^{\circ}$

$\Phi = 0.04 \times 0.5 = 0.02 \text{ Wb}$

Answer: $0.02$ Wb

68709.subject: Physics
68709.text: The amplitude of a damped oscillator becomes $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{\mathrm{rd}}$ of original amplitude in 2 seconds. If its amplitude after 6 second become $\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)$ times the original amplitude, the value of n is ( n is non zero integer)
68709.sol:
The amplitude of a damped oscillator follows $A(t) = A_0 e^{-bt}$, where $A_0$ is the initial amplitude and $b$ is the damping constant.

Given that $A(2) = \frac{A_0}{3}$, substitution yields $\frac{A_0}{3} = A_0 e^{-2b}$, which simplifies to $\frac{1}{3} = e^{-2b}$.

After 6 seconds, $A(6) = \frac{A_0}{n} = A_0 e^{-6b}$, giving $\frac{1}{n} = e^{-6b}$.

Since $e^{-6b} = (e^{-2b})^3 = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{27}$, it follows that $\frac{1}{n} = \frac{1}{27}$.

Thus, $n = 27$.

69714.subject: Physics
69714.text: Consider two rods 1 and 2 of same length. They have different specific heats $(C_1, C_2)$, thermal conductivities $(K_1, K_2)$ and area of cross-section $(A_1, A_2)$ respectively. Both the rods have temperatures $(T_1, T_2)$ at their ends. If their rate of loss of heat due to conduction is equal, then
69714.sol:
The rate of heat flow (or rate of loss of heat due to conduction) through a rod is given by Fourier's law of heat conduction:

$\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{KA(T_1 - T_2)}{L}$

For the first rod, the rate of heat flow is:

$\left(\dfrac{dQ}{dt}\right)_1 = \dfrac{K_1 A_1 (T_1 - T_2)}{L}$

For the second rod, the rate of heat flow is:

$\left(\dfrac{dQ}{dt}\right)_2 = \dfrac{K_2 A_2 (T_1 - T_2)}{L}$

It is given that the rate of loss of heat due to conduction is equal for both rods. Equating the two rates:

$\dfrac{K_1 A_1 (T_1 - T_2)}{L} = \dfrac{K_2 A_2 (T_1 - T_2)}{L}$

Since the length $L$ and the temperature difference $(T_1 - T_2)$ are the same for both rods, they cancel out from both sides:

$K_1 A_1 = K_2 A_2$

Specific heat is not involved in the steady-state rate of heat conduction.

Answer: $A_1 K_1 = A_2 K_2$

70964.subject: Biology
70964.text:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Enzyme)		List II
(Reaction catalyzed)
(A). Alcohol dehydrogenase(I). Transfer of certain groups between two molecules
(B). Sucrase(II). Oxidation and reduction reactions
(C). Glucokinase(III). Structural rearrangements within a molecule
(D). Racemases(IV). Hydrolytic reactions
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
70964.sol:
Alcohol dehydrogenase belongs to the class of oxidoreductases, which catalyze oxidation and reduction reactions. Thus, (A) matches with (II).

Sucrase is a hydrolase enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into glucose and fructose. Thus, (B) matches with (IV).

Glucokinase is a transferase enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group from ATP to glucose. Thus, (C) matches with (I).

Racemases are isomerase enzymes that catalyze structural rearrangements within a molecule to convert one stereoisomer into another. Thus, (D) matches with (III).

The correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

71429.subject: Biology
71429.text: During lactic acid fermentation, pyruvic acid is reduced to lactic acid using one proton and two electrons from ________________.
71429.sol:
During lactic acid fermentation, pyruvic acid is reduced to lactic acid by the enzyme lactate dehydrogenase.

The reducing agent for this reaction is $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$, which is produced during the oxidation steps of glycolysis.

In this process, $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$ donates electrons and a proton to pyruvic acid, getting reoxidized to $\text{NAD}^+$, which is then reused in glycolysis.

Answer: $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$ produced during glycolysis.

Carrier proteins help move substances across membranes with the expenditure of energy.
Concentration gradient must be present for the molecules to be diffused through facilitated diffusion.
71579.sol:
Facilitated diffusion is a type of passive transport where molecules move across the cell membrane with the help of carrier or channel proteins.

Since it is a passive process, it occurs along the concentration gradient and does not require the expenditure of metabolic energy (ATP).

Therefore, the statement that carrier proteins help move substances across membranes with the expenditure of energy is incorrect.

Answer: Carrier proteins help move substances across membranes with the expenditure of energy.

71875.subject: Chemistry
71875.text:
Which of the following salts of weak acids and weak bases on hydrolysis turns red litmus blue?
[K_a$ for acetic acid = 1.8\times10^{-5}$, $K_a$ for hydrofluoric acid = $6.8\times10^{-4}$, $K_a$ for hydrogen cynide = $4.0\times10^{-10}$, $K_a$ for formic acid $1.8\times10^{-4}$ and $K_b$ for ammonium hydroxide = $1.8\times10^{-5}$]
71875.sol:
A salt of a weak acid and a weak base forms a basic solution if the dissociation constant of the base (K_b$) is greater than the dissociation constant of the acid (K_a$). A basic solution turns red litmus blue.

For ammonium acetate: $K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$ and $K_b = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$. Since $K_a = K_b$, the solution is neutral.

For ammonium fluoride: $K_a = 6.8 \times 10^{-4}$ and $K_b = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$. Since $K_a > K_b$, the solution is acidic.

For ammonium cyanide: $K_a = 4.0 \times 10^{-10}$ and $K_b = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$. Since $K_b > K_a$, the solution is basic.

For ammonium formate: $K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ and $K_b = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$. Since $K_a > K_b$, the solution is acidic.

Thus, ammonium cyanide forms a basic solution and turns red litmus blue.

Answer: Ammonium cynide

72035.subject: Chemistry
72035.text: The relationship between $\Delta H$ and $\Delta U$ for the reaction, $\text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{PCl}_5(g)$ is given as
72035.sol:
The given reaction is $\text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{PCl}_5(g)$

The relationship between enthalpy change (\Delta H$) and internal energy change (\Delta U$) is given by the equation:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$

where $\Delta n_g$ is the change in the number of moles of gaseous species.

$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$

$\Delta n_g = 1 - (1 + 1) = -1$

Substituting $\Delta n_g = -1$ in the equation, we get:

$\Delta H = \Delta U - RT$

Answer: $\Delta H = \Delta U - RT$

72058.subject: Chemistry
72058.text: Which of the following processes exhibits that $\Delta U = Q_v$ ?
72058.sol:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = Q + W$.

The work done by the system is $W = -P \Delta V$.

For an isochoric process, the volume remains constant, which means $\Delta V = 0$.

Therefore, the work done $W = 0$.

Substituting this into the first law equation, we get $\Delta U = Q$.

Since the heat is exchanged at constant volume, it is denoted as $Q_v$. Thus, $\Delta U = Q_v$ for an isochoric process.

Answer: Isochoric

72459.subject: Physics
72459.text: The path difference between the two waves $y_1 = a_1\sin \left(\omega$t - $\dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} + \pi\right)$ and y_2 = a_2\cos$\left(\omega t - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} + \phi\right)$ is
72459.sol:
The given wave equations are:

$y_1 = a_1\sin\left(\omega t - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} + \pi\right)$

$y_2 = a_2\cos\left(\omega t - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} + \phi\right)$

To compare the phases, we express $y_2$ in terms of the sine function:

$y_2 = a_2\sin\left(\omega t - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} + \phi + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

The phase of the first wave is $\Phi_1 = \omega t - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} + \pi$

The phase of the second wave is $\Phi_2 = \omega t - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda} + \phi + \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

The phase difference $\Delta \Phi$ between the two waves is:

$\Delta \Phi = \Phi_2 - \Phi_1 = \left(\phi + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \pi = \phi - \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

The relation between path difference $\Delta x$ and phase difference $\Delta \Phi$ is given by:

$\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi} \Delta \Phi$

Substituting the value of $\Delta \Phi$:

$\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi}\left(\phi - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Answer: $\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi}\left(\phi - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

In time clauses introduced by conjunctions such as 'when', 'as soon as', 'before', and 'after', the simple present tense is used to express a future action. The main clause uses the simple future tense.

Therefore, the time clause should be 'When I arrive' and the main clause should be 'I will call you'.

The correct sentence is 'When I arrive, I will call you.'

Answer: When I arrive, I will call you.

76437.subject: Mathematics
76437.text: What is the area of the region bounded by the parabolas $y^2=6(x-1)$ and $y^2=3 x ?$
76437.sol:
Given parabolas are $y^2=6(x-1) \quad \ldots .(1)$ and y^2=3 x....(2)
$\begin{aligned} & y^2=6(x-1) \\ & \Rightarrow 6 x-6=y^2 \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{y^2+6}{6}=\frac{y^2}{6}+1 \end{aligned}$ Also, $\mathrm{y}^2=3 \mathrm{x} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{y}^2}{3}$. Solving (1), (2), $3 \mathrm{x}=6(\mathrm{x}-1)\Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{x}=6 \mathrm{x}-6\Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{x}=6 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=2$. $y^2=6 \Rightarrow y= \pm \sqrt{6}$. $\therefore \quad$ Area $\begin{aligned} & =\int_{-\sqrt{6}}^{\sqrt{6}}\left(\frac{y^2}{6}+1-\frac{y^2}{3}\right) \cdot d y=2 \int_0^{\sqrt{6}}\left(1-\frac{y^2}{6}\right) d y=2\left[y-\frac{y^3}{18}\right]_0^{\sqrt{6}} \\ & =2\left[\sqrt{6}-\frac{(\sqrt{6})^3}{18}\right]=2 \times \frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{3}=\frac{4 \sqrt{6}}{3} \end{aligned}$

76909.subject: Mathematics
76909.text:
Consider the following in respect of a non-singular matrix $M$:
I. $|M^2| = |M|^2$
II. $|M| = |M^{-1}|$
III. $|M| = |M^T|$
How many of the above are correct?
76909.sol:
For a non-singular matrix $M$, $|M| \neq 0$.

Using the property of determinants $|AB| = |A||B|$, we have $|M^2| = |M \cdot M| = |M||M| = |M|^2$. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Using the property $M M^{-1} = I$, taking the determinant on both sides gives $|M M^{-1}| = |I| \Rightarrow |M||M^{-1}| = 1 \Rightarrow |M^{-1}| = \dfrac{1}{|M|}$. Since $|M|$ is not necessarily equal to $\dfrac{1}{|M|}$, Statement II is incorrect.

The determinant of a matrix is always equal to the determinant of its transpose, so $|M| = |M^T|$. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Exactly two of the given statements are correct.

Answer: Two

77177.subject: Mathematics
77177.text:
Passage: Let $\left(e^y\right)^x-y=0$, where $y$ is a function of $x$ whose domain is $(0,10]$.

Question: What is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ equal to ?
77177.sol:
Given equation is $(e^y)^x - y = 0$

$e^{xy} = y$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides:

$xy = \ln(y)$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$y + x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$y = \left( \dfrac{1}{y} - x \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$y = \left( \dfrac{1 - xy}{y} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^2}{1 - xy}$

84347.subject: Zoology
84347.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : Forelimbs of human and bats are homologous.
Reason R : Forelimbs of humans and bats have similar anatomical structure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are true, but $\text{R}$ is not the correct explanation of $\text{A}$
84347.sol:
Homologous organs are those which have the same fundamental anatomical structure and embryonic origin but may perform different functions.

The forelimbs of humans and bats have the same basic structural plan, consisting of the humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, and phalanges. Because they share this similar anatomical structure, they are classified as homologous organs.

Thus, Assertion A is true, Reason R is true, and Reason R is the correct explanation for Assertion A.

Answer: Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$

85017.sol:
Structure Location/Characteristics
Organ of Corti Resting on the basilar membrane is the organ of Corti (organ of hearing). The organ of Corti has about 16,000 hair cells, which are arranged into two groups. The inner group consists of only one row of cells and the outer group consists of multiple rows of cells.
Cochlea Functionally the inner ear is differentiated into vestibular apparatus for the sense of equilibrium and cochlea for the sense of hearing.
Eustachian tube The middle ear is connected to the nasopharynx through the Eustachian tube. This helps in equalizing the air pressure on both sides of the eardrum.
Stapes The base of the stapes lies on the membrane of the oval window (an opening of the cochlea). The middle ear ossicles transmit the sound waves from the tympanum to the oval window of the cochlea.

90823.text: If the graph of the function $f\left(x\right) = ax^{3} + x^{2} + bx + c$ is symmetric about the line $x = 2$, then the value of $a + b$ is equal to
90823.sol:
$f \left(x\right)$ is symmetric about the line $x = 2$
$∴ f \left(2 + x\right) = f \left(2 - x\right)$
$a{\left(2 + x\right)}^{3} + {\left(2 + x\right)}^{2} + b\left(2 + x\right) + c = a{\left(2 - x\right)}^{3} + {\left(2 - x\right)}^{2} + b\left(2 - x\right) + c$
$a\left\{{\left(2 + x\right)}^{3} - {\left(2 - x\right)}^{3}\right\} + \left\{{\left(2 + x\right)}^{2} - {\left(2 - x\right)}^{2}\right\} + b\left\{\left(2 + x\right) - \left(2 - x\right)\right\} = 0$
$a\left\{\left(8 + 12x + 6x^{2} + x^{3}\right) - \left(8 - 12x + 6x^{2} - x^{3}\right)\right\} + 2\left(4x\right) + b\left(2x\right) = 0$
$a\left(24x + 2x^{3}\right) + 8x + 2bx = 0$
$2ax^{3} + \left(24a + 2b + 8\right)x = 0$
Which must be true $∀ x \in \mathbb{R}$
$∴$ it is an identity
$∴ 2a = 0$, $24a + 2b + 8 = 0$
$a = 0, 2b + 8 = 0$
$b = - 4$

95247.subject: Botany
95247.text: The elongated or tube-like cells, with thick, lignified walls and tapering ends are&
95247.sol:
Xylem is made up of four different kinds of elements in which tracheids are oldest, elongated with thick-walled structures. Tracheids are the main xylem elements in a gymnosperm.

4 types of xylem elements are -

$1.$ Tracheids: Elongated cells with tapering ends. Dead cells (no protoplasm) with lignified cell walls.

$2.$ Vessels (Tracheae): Vessel is tubular structure made up of cells (vessel members) joined together end to end. Dead cells (no protoplasm) with lignified cell walls and a large central cavity. Members are interconnected by their perforated end walls. These are characteristic features of angiosperms (gymnosperms lack vessels).

$3.$ Xylem fibers: Elongated cells with tapering ends and obliterated lumen. Dead cells (no protoplasm) with lignified cell walls. These may be septate or aseptate.

$4.$ Xylem parenchyma: Living cells with a thin cell wall made up of cellulose. These store food (starch, oil), tannin, etc. Ray parenchymatous cells also perform radial conduction of water.

100344.subject: Physics
100344.text: The velocity-time ($v$-$t$) graph of a body projected vertically upwards from the ground is a straight line. The graph intersects the velocity axis at $20 \text{ m/s}$ and the time axis at $2 \text{ s}$. What is the ratio of the total distance covered to the magnitude of displacement of the body at $t = 3 \text{ s}$?
100344.sol:
From the given information, the velocity at $t = 0$ is $u = 20 \text{ m/s}$, and the velocity becomes zero at $t = 2 \text{ s}$.

The acceleration is the slope of the $v$-$t$ graph:
$a = \dfrac{0 - 20}{2 - 0} = -10 \text{ m/s}^2$

At $t = 3 \text{ s}$, the velocity is:
$v = u + at = 20 - 10(3) = -10 \text{ m/s}$

The displacement is the net area under the $v$-$t$ graph. The graph forms two triangles with the time axis:
Area from $t = 0$ to $t = 2 \text{ s}$ (above the axis): $A_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 20 = 20 \text{ m}$
Area from $t = 2 \text{ s}$ to $t = 3 \text{ s}$ (below the axis): $A_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times (-10) = -5 \text{ m}$

Magnitude of displacement $= |A_1 + A_2| = |20 - 5| = 15 \text{ m}$

Total distance covered $= |A_1| + |A_2| = 20 + 5 = 25 \text{ m}$

Ratio of distance to displacement $= \dfrac{25}{15} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{3}$

101705.subject: Physics
101705.text: An incompressible, ideal fluid flows steadily through a horizontal pipe of varying circular cross-section. A graph is plotted between the kinetic energy per unit volume ($K$) of the fluid on the y-axis and the radius ($r$) of the pipe on the x-axis. Which of the following best describes the shape of this graph?
options: A straight line with a negative slope
101705.sol:
For the steady flow of an incompressible fluid, the volume flow rate $Q$ is constant.

According to the equation of continuity:
$Q = A v = \pi r^2 v$
$\Rightarrow v = \dfrac{Q}{\pi r^2}$

The kinetic energy per unit volume ($K$) is given by:
$K = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2$

Substituting the expression for $v$:
$K = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho \left(\dfrac{Q}{\pi r^2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{\rho Q^2}{2\pi^2 r^4}$

Since $\rho$ and $Q$ are constants for a given steady flow, we get:
$K \propto \dfrac{1}{r^4}$ or $K \propto r^{-4}$

Thus, the graph between $K$ and $r$ will be a non-linear curve representing an inverse fourth-power relationship.

Answer: A non-linear curve representing $K \propto r^{-4}$

102432.text: A particle of mass $m$ executes simple harmonic motion under a restoring force with force constant $k$ and amplitude $A$. If a graph is plotted with the square of its velocity ($v^2$) on the y-axis and the square of its displacement ($x^2$) from the mean position on the x-axis, a straight line is obtained. The magnitude of the slope of this straight line is equal to :
102432.sol:
For a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the velocity $v$ at a displacement $x$ is given by:

$v^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$

where $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$ is the angular frequency and $A$ is the amplitude.

Rearranging the equation, we get:

$v^2 = -\omega^2 x^2 + \omega^2 A^2$

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, where $y = v^2$ and $x = x^2$, the slope of the line is $-\omega^2$.

The magnitude of the slope is $\omega^2 = \dfrac{k}{m}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{k}{m}$

103219.subject: Physics
103219.text:
Statement 1: Voltage across a battery is always less than its emf. and
Statement 2 : There is always some loss of energy due to internal resistance of the battery.
options: Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True ; Statement-2 is a correct explanation for Statement-1.
Statement- 1 is True, Statement- 2 is True ; Statement-2 is not a correct explanation for Statement-1.
Statement- 1 is True, Statement- 2 is False.
Statement- 1 is False, Statement- 2 is True.
103219.sol:
- Statement 1: Voltage across a battery is always less than its emf.
- This is true in most practical scenarios. The terminal voltage \(V\) of a battery is given by \(V=\mathrm{emf}-I r\), where \(I\) is the current and \(r\) is the internal resistance. When current flows through the circuit, some voltage drop occurs across the internal resistance, making the terminal voltage less than the emf. If no current flows, the terminal voltage is equal to the emf. Therefore, the statement holds true for real batteries under load.
- Statement 2: There is always some loss of energy due to the internal resistance of the battery.
- This is true. When current flows, some energy is dissipated as heat in the internal resistance, which results in energy loss.

103701.subject: Physics
103701.text: An alpha particle is moving with a speed of $10^5 \text{ m/s}$ parallel to a long straight current-carrying conductor. The perpendicular distance between the alpha particle and the conductor is $10 \text{ cm}$. If the alpha particle experiences a magnetic force of $6.4 \times 10^{-19} \text{ N}$, calculate the current flowing in the conductor.
103701.sol:
The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by $F = qvB\sin\theta$.

For an alpha particle, the charge is $q = +2e = 2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C} = 3.2 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.

Since the particle moves parallel to the straight wire, its velocity is perpendicular to the circular magnetic field lines produced by the wire ($\theta = 90^\circ$).

The magnetic field $B$ at the position of the alpha particle is:
$B = \dfrac{F}{qv} = \dfrac{6.4 \times 10^{-19}}{3.2 \times 10^{-19} \times 10^5} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ T}$.

The magnetic field due to a long straight wire is $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$.

Rearranging for the current $I$ and substituting $r = 10 \text{ cm} = 0.1 \text{ m}$:
$I = \dfrac{B \times 2\pi r}{\mu_0} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-5} \times 2\pi \times 0.1}{4\pi \times 10^{-7}}$

$I = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-6}}{4\pi \times 10^{-7}} = 10 \text{ A}$.

Answer: $10 \text{ A}$

103703.subject: Physics
103703.text: A straight conducting wire of a certain length is bent into a single-turn circular loop. When a steady current $I$ is passed through it, the magnetic field produced at its centre is $B$. If the same wire is now rewound into a closely packed circular coil of $n$ turns and the identical current $I$ is passed through it, what will be the new magnetic field at the centre of the coil?
103703.sol:
Let the length of the wire be $L$.

For the single-turn loop, the radius $R_1$ is given by:
$L = 2\pi R_1 \Rightarrow R_1 = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}$

The magnetic field at the centre of this single-turn loop is:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R_1}$

When the same wire is rewound into a coil of $n$ turns, let the new radius be $R_n$. The total length of the wire remains constant:
$L = n(2\pi R_n) \Rightarrow R_n = \dfrac{L}{n(2\pi)} = \dfrac{R_1}{n}$

The new magnetic field at the centre of the $n$-turn coil is:
$B_n = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I}{2R_n}$

Substituting $R_n = \dfrac{R_1}{n}$ into the equation:
$B_n = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I}{2 \left(\dfrac{R_1}{n}\right)} = n^2 \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R_1}\right)$

Since $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R_1}$, we get:
$B_n = n^2 B$

Answer: $n^2 B$

104123.subject: Physics
104123.text: A coil when connected across a steady DC voltage $V$ draws a current $I_0$. When it is connected across an AC source of the same rms voltage $V$ and frequency $f$, it draws an rms current of $\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$. If the frequency of the AC source is increased to $2f$ while keeping the rms voltage constant, what will be the new rms current drawn by the coil?
104123.sol:
When connected to a steady DC voltage $V$, the inductive reactance is zero. The resistance of the coil is $R = \dfrac{V}{I_0}$.

When connected to an AC source of frequency $f$, the impedance is $Z = \dfrac{V}{I_{rms}} = \dfrac{V}{\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}} = \sqrt{2}R$.

Since $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$, we have $\sqrt{2}R = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$, which gives $X_L = R$.

When the frequency is doubled to $2f$, the new inductive reactance becomes $X_L' = 2X_L = 2R$.

The new impedance is $Z' = \sqrt{R^2 + (2R)^2} = \sqrt{5}R$.

The new rms current drawn is $I' = \dfrac{V}{Z'} = \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{5}R} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{5}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{5}}$

108959.subject: Chemistry
108959.text: For the equilibrium reaction $2\text{NO}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4}(\text{g})$, the equilibrium constant $K_{c}$ is $4.0 \times 10^{3}$ at a certain temperature. If the equilibrium concentration of $\text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4}$ is $0.1\text{ M}$, what is the equilibrium concentration of $\text{NO}_{2}$?
108959.sol:
The equilibrium constant expression for the given reaction is:
$K_{c} = \dfrac{[\text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4}]}{[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2}}$

Substitute the given values into the expression:
$4.0 \times 10^{3} = \dfrac{0.1}{[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2}}$

Rearrange to solve for $[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2}$:
$[\text{NO}_{2}]^{2} = \dfrac{0.1}{4.0 \times 10^{3}} = \dfrac{1}{40000} = 25 \times 10^{-6}$

Taking the square root of both sides gives the concentration of $\text{NO}_{2}$:
$[\text{NO}_{2}] = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$

Common mistakes:
- Forgetting to take the square root leads to $2.5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$.
- Inverting the $K_{c}$ expression leads to $20\text{ M}$ or $400\text{ M}$.

Answer: $5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$

117098.subject: Chemistry
117098.text: Heating potassium permanganate produces a green solid (A). When an aqueous solution of (A) is treated with a dilute acid, it undergoes disproportionation to give a purple solution (B) and a brown-black precipitate (C). The oxidation states of manganese in compounds (B) and (C) are respectively:
117098.sol:
When potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) is heated, it decomposes to form potassium manganate, which is the green solid (A).

$2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 \text{ (A)} + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

In an acidic medium, the manganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$) undergoes a disproportionation reaction to form the permanganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^-$), which gives a purple solution (B), and manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$), which is a brown-black precipitate (C).

$3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^- \text{ (B)} + \text{MnO}_2 \text{ (C)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The oxidation state of manganese in the purple solution (B), which contains the permanganate ion, is $+7$.

The oxidation state of manganese in the brown-black precipitate (C), which is $\text{MnO}_2$, is $+4$.

Thus, the oxidation states of manganese in (B) and (C) are $+7$ and $+4$ respectively.

Answer: $+7$ and $+4$

118888.text: Lucas test is given by an alcohol within 5 minutes. $0.22 \mathrm{~g}$ of which liberates $56 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $\mathrm{CH}_4$ at STP on treating with $\mathrm{CH}_3$ MgI. The structure of alcohol is
118888.sol:
Lucas test will be given by all the given alcohols within 5 minutes as all are $2^{\circ}$ alcohols. Exact structure can be known by molecular mass or formula of alcohol which will be obtained as follows :
Let molecular mass of alcohol be $M$.
$\frac{56}{22400}=\frac{0.22}{M}$ or, $M=\frac{22400 \times 0.22}{56}=88$
The general formula of alcohols is $\mathrm{C}_n \mathrm{H}_{2 n+1} \mathrm{OH}$. The molecular mass 88 corresponds to the value of $n=5$. Thus, the $2^{\circ}$ alcohol is $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{CHCHOHCH}_3$.

121331.subject: Botany
121331.text: What happens when two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together in case of Aspergillus , Claviceps and Neurospora?
121331.sol: When a fungus reproduces sexually, <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;">  two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together and fuse. In some fungi the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cells (2n). However, in other fungi (ascomycetes and basidiomycetes), an interveningdikaryotic stage (n + n, i.e., two nuclei per cell) occurs; such a condition is called a dikaryon and the phase is called dikaryophase of fungus. </mark>  Later, the parental nuclei fuse and the cells become diploid. The fungi form fruiting bodies in which reduction division occurs, leading to formation of haploid spores.

122028.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Gymnosperms are characterized by the presence of naked seeds.
Reason (R) : In gymnosperms, the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization.

options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
122028.sol:
Assertion (A) states that gymnosperms have naked seeds, which is a true statement. The term gymnosperm itself means naked seeds (gymnos = naked, sperma = seeds).

Reason (R) states that the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization. This is also true and provides the exact anatomical reason why the seeds (which develop from ovules post-fertilization) are naked.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

122742.subject: Botany
122742.text: In which type of flower is the ovary completely enclosed by the margin of the thalamus?
122742.sol: Based on the position of calyx, corolla and androecium in respect of the ovary on thalamus, the flowers are described as hypogynous, perigynous and epigynous (Figure 5.9). In the hypogynous flower the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior, e.g., mustard, china rose and brinjal. If gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level, it is called perigynous. The ovary here is said to be half inferior, e.g., plum, rose, peach. In epigynous flowers, the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of flower arise above the ovary. Hence, the ovary is said to be inferior as in flowers of guava and cucumber, and the ray florets of sunflower.

125623.subject: Botany
125623.text: In an experiment with isolated chloroplasts from a $C_3$ plant, it is observed that as the ratio of $O_2$ to $CO_2$ in the surrounding medium increases, the formation of a 2-carbon compound increases while the overall sugar yield drops. Which specific property of the primary carboxylating enzyme explains this phenomenon?
options: Competitive binding of $O_2$ and $CO_2$ at the same active site
Allosteric inhibition of the enzyme's activity by high concentrations of $O_2$
Non-competitive inhibition of the enzyme by the newly formed 2-carbon compound
Irreversible denaturation of the enzyme's active site at elevated $O_2$ levels
125623.sol:
The primary carboxylating enzyme in $C_3$ plants is RuBisCO (Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase).

RuBisCO has a single active site that can bind to both $CO_2$ and $O_2$. The binding of these two gases is competitive.

When the ratio of $O_2$ to $CO_2$ increases, $O_2$ successfully competes with $CO_2$ for the active site. This shifts the enzyme's function towards its oxygenase activity.

As a result, RuBP is oxygenated to form a 3-carbon compound (phosphoglycerate) and a 2-carbon compound (phosphoglycolate), initiating the photorespiratory pathway and thereby decreasing the overall sugar yield.

The phenomenon is strictly due to competitive binding at the active site, not allosteric inhibition, non-competitive inhibition, or denaturation.

Answer: Competitive binding of $O_2$ and $CO_2$ at the same active site

125889.subject: Botany
125889.text: Which types of plants primarily use water for the transport of male gametes?
125889.sol: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. As against this, you would recall that water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes among the lower plant groups such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes. It is believed, particularly for some bryophytes and pteridophytes, that their distribution is limited because of the need for water for the transport of male gametes and fertilisation. Some examples of water pollinated plants are Vallisneria and Hydrilla which grow in fresh water and several marine sea-grasses such as Zostera. Not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants.

127577.subject: Botany
127577.text: What is the definition of gross primary productivity (GPP) in an ecosystem?
options: The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis
The rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
127577.sol: A constant input of solar energy is the basic requirement for any ecosystem to function and sustain. Primary production is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight (g m–2) or energy (kcal m–2). The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of gm–2 yr –1 or (kcal m–2) yr–1 to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. It can be divided into gross primary productivity (GPP) and net primary productivity (NPP). Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP). GPP – R = NPP Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers). Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons. Rest of course, is on land. Discuss the main reason for the low productivity of ocean with your teacher.

128029.subject: Zoology
128029.text: Open into cloaca of a female frog (I) 2 oviducts (II) 2 ureters (III) 2 urinogenital ducts (IV) Alimentary canal (V) Bidder canal
128029.sol: The elimination of nitrogenous wastes is carried out by a well developed excretory system. The excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, ureters, cloaca and urinary bladder. These are compact, dark red and bean like structures situated a little posteriorly in the body cavity on both sides of the vertebral column. Each kidney is composed of several structural and functional units called uriniferous tubules of nephrons. Two ureters emerge from the kidneys in the male frogs. The ureters act as urinogenital ducts which open into the cloaca.   The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviducts arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.   The digestive system consists of alimentary canal and digestive glands. The alimentary canal is short because frogs are carnivores and hence the length of intestine is reduced. The mouth opens into the buccal cavity that leads to the oesophagus through pharynx. Oesophagus is a short tube that opens into the stomach which in turn continues as the intestine, rectum and finally opens outside by the cloaca. Liver secretes bile that is stored in the gallbladder. Pancreas, a digestive gland, produces pancreatic juice.

129338.subject: Zoology
129338.text: During the transmission of a nerve impulse across a chemical synapse, what is the immediate physiological consequence of neurotransmitters binding to their specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane?
options: Movement of synaptic vesicles towards the pre-synaptic membrane
Release of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft
Generation of an action potential in the pre-synaptic neuron
129338.sol:
During synaptic transmission at a chemical synapse, the binding of neurotransmitters to their specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane leads to the opening of specific ion channels.

This opening allows the entry of ions, which can generate a new potential (either excitatory or inhibitory) in the post-synaptic neuron.

The movement of synaptic vesicles and the release of neurotransmitters are pre-synaptic events that occur prior to receptor binding, while the action potential in the pre-synaptic neuron is the initial trigger for the entire process.

Answer: Opening of specific ion channels

130567.subject: Zoology
130567.text: What is a significant drawback of natural methods of contraception?
130567.sol: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected. As chances of fertilisation are very high during this period, it is called the fertile period. Therefore, by abstaining from coitus during this period, conception could be prevented. Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination. Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of six months following parturition. As no medicines or devices are used in these methods, side effects are almost nil. Chances of failure, though, of this method are also high.

131512.subject: Zoology
131512.text: Where is the promoter located in a transcription unit?
131512.sol: The promoter and terminator flank the structural gene in a transcription unit. The promoter is said to be located towards the 5' -end (upstream) of the structural gene (the reference is made with respect to the polarity of the coding strand). It is a DNA sequence that provides binding site for RNA polymerase, and it is the presence of a promoter in a transcription unit that also defines the template and coding strands. By switching its position with terminator, the definition of coding and template strands could be reversed. The terminator is located towards the 3' -end (downstream) of the coding strand and it usually defines the end of the process of transcription (Figure 5.9). There are additional regulatory sequences that may be present further upstream or downstream to the promoter. Some of the properties of these sequences shall be discussed while dealing with regulation of gene expression
